stories.headline: US proposes tariffs of up to 20% on 14 economies, including the EU and China

sources.body: The United States on Wednesday unveiled proposed tariffs on 14 economies including the European Union and China, after a months-long probe into alleged excess production -- the latest move by US President Donald Trump to remake Washington's trade relationships. The duties, proposed at up to 20 percent, come over allegations the economies "are promoting production and capacity divorced from the realities of demand and market principles," a senior US official said on condition of anonymity. FRANCE 24's Camille Knight.
sources.headline: US unveils proposed tariffs on major partners, including EU and China

sources.body:
Brazil indignant about proposed tariffs on sugar and aircraft, while Beijing says new levies amount to ‘political manipulation’

Trump proposing new tariffs on 14 partners including China and EU

Brazil has said it will not bend to the new US tariff “threat” and China accused Washington of “political manipulation” in the wake of Donald Trump’s latest economic salvo against 14 major trading partners.

Brazil’s government said on Wednesday: “Brazil will not yield to this type of threat”, adding in its statement that the “unilateral decision constitutes an unacceptable action within the framework of the ongoing bilateral negotiating process”.

It voiced particular indignation at US proposals for higher import taxes for raw and refined sugar and a new 10% tariff on aircraft, a change that would hit Embraer, Brazil’s largest aircraft maker.

It added that Brazil would continue to negotiate “without ruling out the possibility of adopting retaliatory measures in response to the illegal and unjust imposition of tariffs on Brazilian products”.

Brazil was particularly singled out for in the announcement after trade talks stalled. The Trump administration claimed on Wednesday that the new tariffs would be consistent with trade deals that the US reached last year with dozens of countries.

The new tariffs are being imposed under a law which allowed the president to target countries the US had found to engage in unreasonable or discriminatory trade practices. Jamieson Greer, the US trade representative, told CNBC that many US trading partners had adopted “market distorting practices that tilt the trade balance in their favour while eroding America’s manufacturing base.”

The administration will seek feedback from affected industries and hold a hearing on 25 January, suggesting the final duties won’t take effect until February or March.

China is potentially facing one of the biggest hits. The US said China would face the highest capped rate of 20%, which in some cases will be stacked on top of other import taxes for a total rate of 45%. The US and China last year reached a trade truce but that is set to expire on 10 January 2027.

A spokesperson for China’s embassy in Washington rejected allegations that China was ‌a source of ⁠excess capacity, but stopped short of threatening retaliation.

“The so-called issue of ‘industrial overcapacity’ does not really exist and should not be used as a pretext for political manipulation,” the spokesperson said, urging the two sides to jointly deliver on agreements secured between Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping.

Earlier, China’s foreign ministry restated its opposition while calling for the US to resolve the issue through dialogue. “A tariff war or a trade war serves no party’s interests,” spokesperson Guo Jiakun said.

Greer told CNBC that the administration is proposing a “broad exemption” for $30bn worth of Chinese goods in line with the deal. “We’ve talked to our trading partners about this – they know what we’re proposing,” Greer told CNBC. “I think a lot of this is baked in.”
sources.headline: Trump tariff threat ‘unacceptable’, says Brazil, as China denounces levies as baseless

sources.body: The EU said Wednesday that it rejected the premise of new tariffs on its exports proposed by the United States and expected Washington to stick by a deal struck with Brussels last year. The US unveiled proposed tariffs on 14 economies including the European Union and China, after a months-long probe into alleged excess production. FRANCE 24's Dave Keating reports from Brussels.
sources.headline: EU says 'strongly' rejects premise of new US tariffs

stories.headline: Houthis attack Saudi Red Sea ports as missiles are intercepted over Riyadh

sources.body:
Explosion reported in Sanaa after Saudi air defenses intercept ballistic missiles targeting Riyadh.

Yemen’s Houthi group has struck the port of Jizan on Saudi Arabia’s Red Sea coast as fighting intensifies near the Yemeni city of Taiz.

A Saudi-led military coalition said a Houthi attack on Jizan caused only minor damage and no civilian casualties on Wednesday, adding that “efforts are underway to determine the type of projectile” used.

The spokesman for the coalition, Turki al-Maliki, later said in a statement on X that its forces intercepted and destroyed a Houthi drone over Jeddah’s port in Saudi Arabia.

No civilian injuries were reported from falling debris following the interception, he added.

After the coalition’s statement, an explosion was heard in Yemen’s capital, Sanaa, according to Al Jazeera’s Nabil al-Yousfi.

The Saudi-led coalition then said its air defences intercepted and destroyed ballistic missiles launched by the Houthis towards Saudi Arabia’s capital, Riyadh.

The attempted strike on the capital follows a Houthi drone attack on a skyscraper in Riyadh’s financial district on Tuesday, injuring at least 11 people .

The latest incidents mark a further escalation between the Iran-aligned Houthis and Saudi Arabia, including strikes from both sides targeting airports, energy facilities and other civilian and economic infrastructure.

The strikes on Saudi Arabian ports come after the Houthi-affiliated Al Masirah TV reported new Saudi attacks on the port of Hodeidah in Yemen .

Earlier on Wednesday, the Houthis threatened to attack Saudi ports if Hodeidah came under attack.

“The port of Hodeidah handles 90 percent of imported goods into Yemen. If it is closed, it could bring the humanitarian situation to the brink of collapse”, said Al Jazeera’s Yousef Mawry, reporting from Yemen’s capital, Sanaa.

“Some of Saudi Arabia’s recent attacks at the Port of Hodeidah have targeted storage tanks and cranes used to load and unload shipments”, Mawry said.

Yemen’s internationally recognised government forces have been battling the Houthis on several fronts, with the army’s spokesman saying 654 strikes have been carried out against the group on Wednesday.

Yemen’s western front has witnessed the heaviest concentration of recent strikes, according to Al Jazeera’s Maha Ali, reporting from Taiz.

Government forces have said air strikes targeted Houthi positions west of Taiz.

“These strikes are part of an intense and sustained wave of air raids that have continued for approximately 72 hours”, Ali said.

“Particular attention is focused on the most significant mountain range overlooking central Taiz: Jabal Saber and its highest peak, Jabal al-Arus. The government says the Houthis want to seize this strategic peak”, she added.

The Houthis said there have been 105 air strikes and missile attacks by the Saudi-led coalition targeting civilian sites in Sanaa and 10 governorates on Wednesday.
sources.headline: Houthis target Saudi Arabia’s Red Sea ports as strikes escalate

stories.headline: US approves SpaceX plan for up to one million satellites to host orbital data centers

sources.body:
US regulators have given SpaceX the go-ahead to launch a million satellites into Earth's orbit to help build data centres in space - the first approval of its kind.

The company, which is owned by Elon Musk, wants to use sunlight to power satellites that will process data for AI and send the results back to Earth.

The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) said on Wednesday that the project, known as Starmind, will "support America's booming super intelligence economy".

Its approval comes as communities across the US have pushed back against the expansion of data centres on the ground.

Space X believes the "orbital data centres" are the most cost and energy-efficient way to meet the growing demand for artificial intelligence (AI) computing power that is beyond "terrestrial capabilities".

FCC Chairman Brendan Carr said in a statement that the project "opens a bold new frontier for the computing infrastructure needed to power America's leadership and growth".

"This is the kind of American ingenuity that can unite our strengths in space and advanced technology, reinforce our economic leadership, and expand prosperity here at home," Carr said.

Responding to the announcement, Musk wrote on X: "Much appreciated. This will be a great asset to America and the world."

Under the FCC licence, deployment of the satellites has to begin no later than November 2033. SpaceX will be required to have deployed 10% by November 2035, rising to 50% by November 2038.

The company has already said it wants to launch its first Starmind satellite next year.

Its unclear if a million satellites will be launched or if SpaceX has sought approval for a higher number than it will use.

Like SpaceX's current Starlink network, which provides high-speed internet via more than 10,000 satellites, Starmind's satellites will operate in low-Earth orbit at altitudes ranging between 500-2,000km (310-1,242 miles).

Starmind's satellites will communicate with Starlink's and then relay the data to Earth.

The solar-powered satellite system "promises to bring the human race closer to a Kardashev II civilisation—one that can harness the full power of the sun", the FCC statement said, in a reference to a hypothetical society, proposed by an astronomer in the 1960s, capable of harnessing the entire energy output of its home star.

The orbiting data centre concept is also being explored by other firms - including Google and Blue Origin - and is being pitched as a greener alternative to traditional centres, which require enormous amounts of power to run and water for cooling.

The ever-expanding use of AI computing has seen a massive increase in the amount of data that needs to be stored and processed around the world.

New facilities continue to be built but it is becoming difficult to find places to put them. Data centres are large and sprawling, use enormous amounts of power and water for cooling, and increasingly local people don't want them built nearby.

Data centres were a central issue in the midterm elections earlier in November, with many Democratic candidates promising tougher regulation on their construction.
sources.headline: US approves SpaceX plan to send a million data satellites to space

sources.body: The US Federal Communications Commission has approved SpaceX's plan to deploy up to one million satellites to build data centers in orbit, giving Elon Musk's company a major foothold in the industry. The authorization runs through 2040, as tech firms race to move computing infrastructure into space despite significant technical hurdles.
sources.headline: US authorizes SpaceX to launch up to one million satellites for orbital data centers

stories.headline: Poland plans no-fly zone near Ukraine after repeated airspace violations blamed on Russia

sources.body: Poland will soon create a no-fly zone near the Ukrainian border, a deputy defence minister announced on Wednesday, after several incursions into its airspace it blamed on Russia. Poland backs Ukraine as it fights off Russia's near five-year invasion and has repeatedly accused Moscow of seeking to target Kyiv's supporters with drone incursions and other methods. The no-fly zone is intended to allow Polish forces to quickly identify any Russian military aircraft and shoot them down if necessary. FRANCE 24's Selina Sykes reports.
sources.headline: Poland says will create no-fly zone at Ukraine border after repeated airspace violations

stories.headline: Israeli judges recommend dropping a bribery case against Netanyahu

sources.body:
Judges in Israel have suggested prosecutors drop bribery charges against Benjamin Netanyahu, potentially handing the caretaker prime minister a boost as he fights for his political survival.

The judges told the attorney general that there was little chance of conviction in the first of three cases he is facing, in which he is accused of granting government favours in exchange for positive media coverage.

They also questioned whether his actions amounted to criminal conduct in a second corruption case, and suggested prosecutors seek a plea deal in a third.

Netanyahu has consistently denied the allegations against him and called on Wednesday for the trial to be ended "immediately".

"Ten years of terrible suffering for me, my family, my son," he said in a televised statement.

"Ten years of incitement to hatred that wounds the soul."

Netanyahu was first charged in 2019, but court proceedings have been prolonged in part by the recent Israel-Gaza war.

The case now under serious doubt, known as Case 4,000, concerns an alleged "reciprocal arrangement" between Netanyahu and the controlling shareholder in Israel's biggest telecoms company. Both denied any wrongdoing.

In a highly unusual step, a judging panel at the Jerusalem District Court summoned Israeli Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara on Wednesday to express their concerns.

"The chances of conviction are low – to an extent that warrants reconsidering the matter," Judge Rivka Friedman-Feldman told her, Israeli media reported.

The judges also cast doubt on whether Netanyahu's actions, which are subject to a second case – concerning another alleged quid-pro-quo with another media baron, known as Case 2,000 – met the threshold for criminality.

While they left open the possibility of a conviction in the third case: Case 1,000, which alleges Netanyahu acted for the benefit of an Australian billionaire after being gifted cigars and champagne by him.

However, the judges told the attorney general that, in the public interest, there needed to be a "rethink" in how the trial should move forward, Israeli media report.

Baharav-Miara said she would consider the judges' recommendations.

It has been six years since Netanyahu became Israel's first sitting prime minister to face a criminal trial.

He has always claimed to be the victim of a political witch-hunt and said on Wednesday that the "fabricated cases" against him were now falling apart.

The cases have continued to progress in court while Netanyahu remained in power throughout the war in Gaza, though judges agreed to reduce the number of hearings due to security concerns around the conflict.

The accusations against him have rocked Israeli politics, fuelling already deep divisions. His trial has coincided with controversial, far-reaching judiciary reforms by Netanyahu's government.

For his opponents, Netanyahu's fear of prison has distorted his decision-making as prime minister and made him especially dependent on his far-right coalition partners to remain in power.

This latest development will give a boost to Netanyahu, whose political opponent Gadi Eisenkot is currently attempting to form a coalition government after an inconclusive general election last month.
sources.headline: Israeli judges recommend dropping most serious charges against Netanyahu

sources.body: Judges in the long-running corruption trial of Israeli caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu handed his defence a major boost on Wednesday in recommending the prosecution drop one of the cases in which he is accused of bribery. The recommendations, which came as Israel's longest-serving prime minister fights for his political survival, were immediately cheered by Netanyahu's right-wing allies who demanded the trial be brought to an end. FRANCE 24's Noga Tarnopolsky reports from Jerusalem.
sources.headline: In boost for Netanyahu, judges question corruption trial charges

stories.headline: Fuel tanker crash and fire kill at least 31 people on Cairo highway

sources.body:
Blaze on ring road surrounding Egyptian capital injures at least 21 people and leaves cars and motorcycles charred

A crash involving a fuel tanker ignited a huge fire on a highway surrounding Cairo on Wednesday, killing at least 31 people, Egyptian authorities said.

The blaze on the ring road, a key artery that encircles the Egyptian capital, also injured at least 21 people and left more than two dozen cars and motorcycles charred, according to the latest figures released by the health ministry.

State media reported that the fire broke out when the fuel truck overturned. The stretch of the highway where it occurred was in Waraq, a densely populated neighbourhood in Giza, part of the Greater Cairo area, the health ministry said.

At the scene, rescue workers were pulling people out of burning cars. An Associated Press video showed firefighters working to put out the fire spreading among the cars. Hundreds of people gathered near the scene.

Ahmed Sameer, who was stuck in traffic as the road was blocked after the accident, saw the fuel truck and many cars on fire. He said he saw at least eight bodies being removed from burned cars.

“It was a huge fire, the cars got stuck together because of the fire,” he said, describing the fear and panic that followed. “It was a shocking scene.”

The Egyptian president, Abdel Fatah al-Sisi, expressed his condolences to the victims in a statement. The public prosecutor’s office said DNA investigations were under way to identify the victims.

The health minister, Khaled Abdel Ghaffar, said the injured were taken to nearby hospitals and that he would head to the scene. He said the death toll was preliminary, raising concerns it could rise further.

Deadly traffic incidents claim thousands of lives every year in Egypt, which has a poor transportation safety record. Speeding, bad roads and poor enforcement of traffic laws are the main reasons behind most of the crashes.

In January, 21 people were killed and 16 were injured in a multicar pileup on a road near the southern province of Beni Suef.
sources.headline: At least 31 killed as fuel tanker crash ignites large fire on Cairo highway

sources.body: At least 31 people were killed and 15 injured when a fuel truck overturned and burst into flames on a busy highway in Cairo on Wednesday, engulfing nearby vehicles, Egyptian authorities said.
sources.headline: At least 31 killed in Cairo fire after fuel truck overturns on busy highway

stories.headline: Major East Coast storm forces New York’s Thanksgiving parade to move to Saturday

sources.body: A powerful storm forecast to bring fierce winds and heavy rain to the northeastern United States has forced the unprecedented postponement of the city's 100th annual Thanksgiving Day Parade, with the event rescheduled for Saturday. Officials warned that Thursday's conditions could bring down tree limbs and power lines, while posing a safety risk to the parade's giant balloons and the crowds below.
sources.headline: Powerful US storm forces historic postponement of New York's Thanksgiving Day Parade

sources.body: A major storm is expected to hit the East Coast on Thursday.
sources.headline: Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade postponed by storm, rescheduled for Saturday

sources.body: <p>Las encuestas se apagaron este lunes dejando esta foto: el PP es primero con el 31,4% de los votos en promedio, seguido del PSOE (29,1%), Vox (17,9%) y los Frentes, la suma de Frente Amplio y coaliciones con Podemos y otras fuerzas (6,8%). La tendencia de la campaña es un PSOE que crece: la ventaja del PP sobre los socialistas se ha reducido de casi seis puntos a poco más de dos. stories.headline: El Hierro declares emergency after more than 2,000 migrant arrivals in a day; military emergency unit deployed

sources.body:
Noves arribades de migrants aquest dimecres a l'illa canària d'El Hierro, amb 190 persones rescatades. En les últimes 24 hores, hi han arribat més de 2.000 migrants, la xifra més alta en un sol dia que s'ha registrat mai a tot l'Estat per via marítima.

En més de 30 anys d'història d'aquesta ruta migratòria, no s'havien fet mai tants rescats per mar durant una jornada com els que s'han produït aquest dimarts.

El govern de les Canàries ha declarat l'emergència sanitària a l'illa "per la situació excepcional de caràcter sanitari, social i de seguretat", des de les 15.00 d'aquest dimecres.

A més, el president canari, Fernando Clavijo, ha demanat formalment el desplegament de la Unitat Militar d'Emergències (UME) a El Hierro per ajudar a garantir la seguretat a l'illa. Segons ha dit, la situació "és insostenible" i l'UME els ha adjudar "des del punt de vista migratori i sanitari". El Ministeri de Defensa ha explicat que prepara l'enviament d'efectius, però encara no n'ha precisat la xifra.

Salvament Marítim ha interceptat 14 pasteres, i en total al mes de novembre han arribat a l'arxipèlag unes 14.000 persones , la majoria, a aquesta petita illa de només 12.000 habitants.

Francis Mendoza , coordinador de Corazón Naranja, una associació de voluntaris que atén els migrants, ha explicat al "Catalunya nit" de Catalunya Ràdio com han viscut sobre el terreny atendre un volum tan alt de persones.

La situació, per a aquesta illa tan petita, és una mica desbordant.

Mendoza assegura que els migrants " arriben molt adolorits, amb diferents ferides " i que la majoria són joves, incloses moltes dones i criatures. De fet, dels milers de persones que han arribat a l'illa en les últimes hores, al voltant de 200 són dones i hi ha més d'un centenar de menors .

Els més petits són un nadó de quatre mesos i una nena de només quatre dies de vida que va néixer en alta mar durant la ruta migratòria i que va ser socorreguda en una de les pasteres a 70 quilòmetres d'El Hierro. Entre els rescatats, també hi havia una persona morta.

El coordinador d'aquesta entitat també creu que hi ha discursos polítics que "s'intenten aprofitar de la situació" . I demana solucions perquè els migrants no es vegin abocats a "abandonar-ho tot i pujar en aquestes barques de fusta amb l'esperança d'arribar a terra, ja que molt d'ells no hi arriben ".

Entre els rescatats aquest dimarts, hi ha nacionalitats de set països africans (Gàmbia, Senegal, Guinea Conakry –o República de Guinea–, Guinea-Bissau, Burkina Faso, Mauritània i Mali) i un refugiat del Iemen.

El president de les Canàries ha qualificat la situació de "tristament històrica"​.​

En una entrevista aquest dimarts a la Cadena SER, Fernando Clavijo ha incidit en el "fracàs" de la "cooperació" entre el Ministeri d'Exteriors i Europa i els països d'origen dels migrants. I ha destacat que "se segueix sense desplegar el Frontex" en aquestes costes mentre les condicions per navegar són "bones".

En aquest sentit, ha atribuït a la Comissió Europea la responsabilitat de "desplegar" tota la seva "capacitat diplomàtica".
sources.headline: El Hierro declara l'emergència per l'arribada de més de 2.000 migrants en un dia i mobilitza l'UME

sources.body:
El Hierro reciibió ayer a más de 2.000 inmigrantes en 14 cayucos, entre ellos un fallecido y una niña de cuatro días 

El Gobierno desplegará la Unidad Militar de Emergencias (UME) en El Hierro para ayudar a garantizar la seguridad sanitaria en la crisis migratoria que sufre la isla, según confirman fuentes gubernamentales a La Vanguardia .

El presidente de Canarias, Fernando Clavijo, había solicitado formalmente el desplazamiento militar dada la situación insostenible de desborde de todos los recursos y medios” ante la llegada de casi 3.000 inmigrantes en cayucos en los últimos dos días . La solicitud consiste en la instalación de un hospital de campaña con los equipos auxiliares correspondientes.

El Gobierno de Canarias, a través de la Dirección General de Emergencias, ha declarado la emergencia por la situación excepcional de carácter sanitario, social y de seguridad en El Hierro a partir de las 15:00 horas de este miércoles a causa de la llegada masiva de personas migrantes por vía marítima. Según fuentes policiales, hasta las 16:00 horas, el mes de noviembre suma 15.560 llegadas irregulares en 151 embarcaciones (128 de ellos a El Hierro). El récord histórico de desembarcos en un mes estaba en casi 16.000 en 2023.

“Me he visto en la necesidad de activarlo y solicitar el apoyo de la UME, desde el punto de vista migratorio y desde el punto de vista sanitario”, argumenta Fernando Clavijo. En concreto, el Gobierno canario ha declarado una emergencia de nivel 2, en la que cabe solicitar apoyo del Estado. El presidente canario ha lamentado “la falta de previsión” y desea que “esta situación se reconduzca lo antes posible”.

El Hospital Insular Nuestra Señora de los Reyes, el único centro con el que cuenta la isla de 12.000 habitantes, cuenta con una veintena de camas, por lo que el repunte migratoria ha obligado a habilitar espacios adicionales. El Hierro también cuenta con dos centros de salud y dos consultorios locales, que no son suficientes para prestar la asistencia sanitaria.

stories.headline: Puigdemont announces December 12 return to Catalunya after Supreme Court applies amnesty

sources.body:
L'expresident Carles Puigdemont tornarà a Catalunya el 12 de desembre. Ho farà, ha dit, "sense haver de demanar permís i perdó i sense haver renunciat a res", després que el Tribunal Suprem li hagi aplicat l'amnistia .

Puigdemont ho ha anunciat des de Brussel·les des del mateix lloc on va comparèixer l'octubre del 2017 –poc després de la declaració d'independència– per anunciar que s'establia a Bèlgica .

Carles Puigdemont anuncia en una roda de premsa des de Brussel·les que tornarà a Catalunya el 12 de desembre al migdia https://t.co/0ZVbKAu5Dd https://t.co/Ac3D5oziVl

El mateix expresident ha anunciat que tornarà en avió des de Brussel·les directament a Barcelona i, un cop a Catalunya, el primer que farà serà dirigir-se al Parlament de Catalunya , on el seu escó continua buit des de les eleccions del 2024.

L'expresident, que ja va anunciar que tornaria a Catalunya després de les eleccions generals de diumenge, ha tingut paraules d'agraïment per al seu equip d'advocats i per a la justícia europea , de la qual ha destacat la seva "garantia d'independència".

Puigdemont ha insistit en la "derrota" i el "fracàs" que, segons ell, representarà per a l'estat espanyol el seu retorn a Catalunya. "L'estat espanyol ha renunciat al seu propòsit d' empresonar i humiliar el qui per a ells és la màxima representació de la derrota de l'1 d'octubre del 2017", ha assegurat.

"A contracor de les autoritats judicials, i amb l'oposició activa de Vox i el PP, la política torna a la política ", ha resumit Carles Puigdemont, que ha volgut deixar clar que tornarà "amb la dignitat institucional que em vaig comprometre a protegir".

En la seva compareixença davant la premsa, Puigdemont ha dit que participarà en el primer ple del Parlament després del seu retorn el 16 de desembre i prendrà la paraula , però ha evitat dir quin paper assumirà en el futur, si renunciarà a l'escó immediatament o si el mantindrà un temps.

"El que jo faré després políticament és difícil de precisar ara mateix", ha dit l'expresident, que ha assegurat que abans de prendre cap decisió vol fer un procés d'escolta i de prendre el pols de la societat catalana després de 9 anys de vida lluny de Catalunya.

En aquest sentit, l'expresident també ha anunciat una conferència a Catalunya el 17 de desembre, en què exposarà la seva visió per "actualitzar l'estratègia per a la independència de Catalunya" en vista de la "metamorfosi" que viu el món.

El que no té data encara és la reunió amb el president de la Generalitat, Salvador Illa , que ha expressat reiteradament la seva intenció de rebre Puigdemont, com ho ha fet amb tots els expresidents.

El Tribunal Suprem ha amnistiat definitivament Carles Puigdemont aquesta setmana. Ho ha fet després que el jutge instructor, Pablo Llarena, tanqués la causa contra ell en aplicació de la llei d'amnistia.

El pas del Suprem ha arribat dos anys i mig després de l'aprovació de l'amnistia al Congrés, un període marcat per les reticències dels tribunals a l'hora d'aplicar el text pactat entre els socialistes, Junts i ERC.
sources.headline: Puigdemont tornarà el 12 de desembre al Parlament: "Ho faré sense demanar perdó ni renunciar a res"

sources.body:
El expresidente catalán y líder del partido Junts per Catalunya, Carles Puigdemont, en rueda de prensa en el Club de Prensa de Bruselas. EFE/EPA/OLIVIER HOSLET

El expresident catalán y líder de Junts, Carles Puigdemont , ha afirmado este miércoles que retornará a su país "sin renunciar a nada " este 12 de diciembre y acudirá directamente al Parlament. "España ha fracasado en su propósito y volveré a mi país, Cataluña, sin tener que pedir permiso, ni perdón, sin haber renunciado a nada", 3.315 días después de ser " destituido ilícitamente de la Generalitat por la aplicación del artículo 155 de la Constitución, acordada por el PP y por el PSOE", según ha asegurado en una rueda de prensa en Bruselas, después de que el Tribunal Supremo decidiera dejar archivada la causa del procés en aplicación de la ley de amnistía, dando así el paso definitivo para que pueda regresar a España y presentarse a unas elecciones .

"Me fui como presidente de la Generalitat y regresaré allí donde la democracia catalana elige o destituye a sus presidentes, que es el Parlament de Cataluña, y lo haré el sábado 12 de diciembre, a mediodía, y esa noche ya podré dormir en casa con mi familia", ha señalado nueve años después de su huida a Bélgica, que ha calificado como "exilio ", con cuatro de sus entonces consellers, Clara Ponsatí, Toni Comín, Lluís Puig y Meritxell Serret —la primera exconsellera en beneficiarse de la ley de amnistía—.

Su regreso a Cataluña llegará tras la que ha calificado como " represión feroz contra el movimiento democrático y pacífico por la independencia de Cataluña", cuando el Estado español ha renunciado "a su propósito de encarcelar y humillar " a quienes para ellos son "la máxima representación" de la "derrota que sufrieron" en el referéndum del 1 de octubre de 2017, ilegalizado por el Tribunal Constitucional.

Carles Puigdemont: "España ha fracaso en su propuesto y volveré a mi país, a Cataluña, sin tenerles que pedir permiso ni perdón. Sin haber renunciado a nada" https://t.co/YG2YEjG94v https://t.co/qKHHJTDWXr

"Decidimos venir al exilio para dar una oportunidad a la resistencia frente a la voracidad represora de todos los poderes españoles que se había desatado y poderlo derrotar", según ha señalado el líder independentista, dando así comienzo a "un recorrido en condiciones muy adversas de lucha contra un Estado" que había hecho de su encarcelamiento "una prioridad nacional".

La decisión del Supremo de aplicar la amnistía a los tres miembros del Ejecutivo catalán que quedaban pendientes —además de Puigdemont, Toni Comín y Lluís Puig— se ha producido, según ha recordado del expresident , pese a la "oposición activa de Vox y del PP", y con este paso la que " la política retorna a la política ".

El expresident ha confirmado que asistirá al pleno de la semana siguiente a su regreso , en el que ha expresado su voluntad de intervenir, y ha avanzado que el jueves 17 de diciembre pronunciará una conferencia abierta al público en la que expondrá su propuesta para adaptar la estrategia del movimiento independentista al nuevo contexto político y jurídico.

sources.body: Spain's Supreme Court has applied a controversial amnesty law to former Catalan separatist leader Carles Puigdemont, closing criminal proceedings against him over his role in the region's failed 2017 independence bid. The ruling, which comes ahead of a snap general election on Sunday, marks the final step in the implementation of the amnesty law, passed by parliament in 2024.
sources.headline: Top Spanish court closes case against Catalan separatist leader
